value.content:
# Page window

This dependency-free library selects one page from a slice. Run its tests with
`cargo test --offline --locked`.

`page(items, offset, limit)` returns up to `limit` consecutive items, starting at
`offset`. Preserve input order and return a borrowed slice. An offset at or past
the end returns an empty page, as does a zero limit. All `usize` offsets and
limits are valid; the function must not panic or wrap arithmetic at large values.

The tests currently fail. Repair the implementation while preserving this
contract. Add focused regression coverage in `tests/regression.rs` before
changing `src/lib.rs`. Keep the existing tests and package configuration intact.

choice.text: Cause: `page` computes `offset + limit` (which can overflow) and slices `items[offset..end]` without clamping `offset` to `items.len()`, so an offset past the end panics instead of yielding an empty page.

arguments.justification: Asserts the documented contract: offsets at or past the end give an empty page, and large offsets/limits must not panic or wrap. Fails against unchanged source, which slices with an unclamped offset and an overflowing offset+limit.

**Cause:** `page` computed `let end = (offset + limit).min(items.len())` and sliced `&items[offset..end]`. Neither the start index nor the addition was guarded, so:
- an `offset` past the end (e.g. `5` on a 3-element slice) indexed out of range and panicked, and
- a large `limit` (e.g. `usize::MAX`) overflowed the addition, violating the documented "must not panic or wrap arithmetic at large values".

**Regression** (`tests/regression.rs`, approved and applied): two tests asserting the intended contract — offsets at/past the end (including `usize::MAX` and an empty slice) return an empty page, and huge limits return the tail without overflowing. **Repair** (`src/lib.rs`, approved and applied): clamp `start = offset.min(items.len())` and use `start.saturating_add(limit).min(items.len())` for the end, keeping order, borrowing, and zero-limit behavior unchanged.

**Final validation: accepted.** `pagination` 3 passed / 0 failed, `regression` 2 passed / 0 failed, `rustfmt --check` clean, and the independent contract oracle passed across all length/offset/limit combinations (including `usize::MAX`), always returning borrowed, order-preserving slices.
